hypnosis_quote: Breathe in small amounts through your nose and let it out quietly, through your nose too.
source_quote: By simply pursing your lips together on exhale, you can slow down your exhale. Slower exhales, combined with not breathing more on inhales, lead to overall reduction in breathing.
why: The two guides give different instructions for the same named practice: here small breaths in and out through the nose, there a slowed out-breath through pursed lips with the in-breath left as it is, so a reader of both can't tell which is the method.
what: The sentence on how to breathe in and out (nose both ways): keep it, replace it, or give both ways.

hypnosis_quote: However, please don’t hold your breath until you are air hungry, which can make you more anxious in the short term.
source_quote: That slight oxygen hunger feels a bit anxiogenic for the first 20 seconds or so, but after that, you’ll feel much calmer.
why: This guide says to avoid air hunger (it warns against holding the breath that far) and to stop if panicky, while the source, which never mentions holds or pauses, says a slight hunger for air is expected, feels a little anxious for about 20 seconds and then calms, so a reader here stops at the point where the source says to carry on.
what: The bracketed warning about air hunger and the last sentence of the section (when to stop): whether slight air hunger is expected, and for how long.

hypnosis_quote: With EFT (Emotional Freedom Techniques, or tapping), you tap gently on your body while you say something like, “Even though I have this anxiety, I am willing to be kind to the part of me that is afraid,” and you stay with what you feel.
source_quote: The Emotional Freedom Technique (EFT) is a very simple anytime anywhere practice that only takes a few seconds or minutes of just lightly tapping on different parts of you head (NOT with a hammer!).
why: This guide says to tap "on your body" without saying where or for how long, and the source says the head, for a few seconds to a few minutes, so a reader here can't start from this sentence alone.
what: First sentence of the section: where to tap (body or head) and for how long.

hypnosis_quote: If you would like more information about somatic experiencing, or even a free intro session, please see my somatic guide .
source_quote: As mentioned at the top, as a paid subscriber on my substack, you’re eligible for one free SE intro session with Hâle.
why: This guide offers "a free intro session" with no condition, and the source says it is one session, for paid subscribers, given by Hâle, so a free reader is told to expect something they won't get.
what: First sentence of the section: who the free session is for (paid subscribers, one session).

hypnosis_quote: So you might start by tracking, by discovering where the activation is, where a neutral place is, and then whether you can move your attention from one to the other, very slowly, like a snail.
source_quote: He uses the concepts of titration (going from the shallow end of the pool slowly deeper), pendulation (going in and out of the deep end to learn safety there), and orientation (coming out of the pool, drying off, noticing you’re safe).
why: The exercise here ends with attention moving between the activated place and the neutral one, and the source has a third step after that, orientation (coming out and noticing you're safe), so the reader is given no way to finish.
what: After the last sentence of the section: one sentence for the closing step (orientation).

hypnosis_quote: Maybe get a massage, or massage a foot, your scalp, a temple, or the back of the neck, the top of a shoulder, etc.
source_quote: Some massage therapies are super aggressive in that domain, like Rolfing , some are fairly aggressive still like Deep Tissue, some are medium-aggressive, like Thai massage, and some, like Swedish Massage, are quite gentle. Choose the level that feels right for you.
why: The passage is about calming an over-activated body and says only "get a massage", and the source says styles run from very forceful (Rolfing, deep tissue) to gentle (Swedish) and to choose the level, which a reader booking a massage to calm down needs to know.
what: At "Maybe get a massage": a few words on choosing a gentle style, or a link to the source's massage section.

hypnosis_quote: Work in this order – first your body, then your inner child, then some inquiry, then some action:
source_quote: If you’re one of those people who finds that none of these therapies work on you, you should consider brain health and neuro-inflammation first.
why: The source now puts a step ahead of the body work for readers on whom none of it works (sleep, medication, nutrition, brain inflammation, with links to the sleep and de-armoring guides), and the working order here starts at the body and, in these sections, gives such a reader nowhere to go.
what: At the working-order sentence: a pointer for readers the body steps don't help (first check the rest of the guide doesn't already say it).

hypnosis_quote: A 2025 systematic review found 7 randomized controlled trials for anxiety disorders, and noted that EFT was more effective than no intervention in several of them, though it isn't one of the first-line therapies for anxiety.
source_quote: It’s not a cure for trauma, but it is a nice present-moment re-orienting button.
why: This guide limits EFT only by its evidence for anxiety, and the source says what it is for (a quick way to re-orient in the present) and that it doesn't cure trauma, which tells the reader what to expect from it.
what: End of the section, beside the first-line-therapies clause: the source's limit (no cure, a present-moment reset).

hypnosis_quote: There isn’t a ton of evidence for EFT, but there are some studies on anxiety.
source_quote: It helps with all kinds of situations.
why: The same author hedges EFT here (little evidence, no first-line therapy) and promises more in the source (helps with all kinds of situations, "comes to the rescue"), and this guide is the more careful of the two, so nothing here should be carried over without his say.
what: The evidence sentences stay as they are; ask whether the two guides should make the same strength of claim.

hypnosis_quote: If you would like more information about somatic experiencing, or even a free intro session, please see my somatic guide .
source_quote: SE is a therapy you can do for yourself, but it really helps if you have a therapist first, as with most other therapies.
why: This guide gives the tracking exercise as something to do alone and mentions a session only as an extra, and the source says doing it alone goes better after a therapist has shown you.
what: First sentence of the section, with the intro-session mention: that a therapist first helps.

hypnosis_quote: So you might start by tracking, by discovering where the activation is, where a neutral place is, and then whether you can move your attention from one to the other, very slowly, like a snail.
source_quote: Somatic Experiencing can include some bodily shaking if that is what your body seems to want to do for completing the original activation energy.
why: A reader who starts to tremble while tracking the activated place isn't told that shaking can be part of Somatic Experiencing and may be what the body wants.
what: After the tracking sentence: one sentence on shaking, or a link to the source's shaking section.

hypnosis_quote: In somatic experiencing (SE), you are not digging into the trauma.
source_quote: While Levine doesn’t use self-hypnosis in his SE, he has mentioned it can be a valuable fit if done right, which is why I’ve integrated SE into my self-hypnosis guide and app.
why: The source now says its founder doesn't use self-hypnosis in Somatic Experiencing and that the pairing is the author's own, and this guide presents its exercise as Somatic Experiencing without saying so.
what: Where the section introduces SE: whether to say the pairing with self-hypnosis is his own.

hypnosis_quote: Maybe get a massage, or massage a foot, your scalp, a temple, or the back of the neck, the top of a shoulder, etc.
source_quote: On the other hand, not everyone enjoys a massage, and some people are repulsed by being touched. I’d say first try giving yourself a massage, which is also a lot cheaper usually.
why: This guide puts getting a massage first and your own hands second, and the source says to try your own hands first because some people can't bear being touched, a reason this guide doesn't give.
what: The "Maybe get a massage" sentence: the order of the two options, and the reason.

source_quote: There’s also a type of breathwork that synergizes with sound to help you connect with your emotions, called Zensing :
why: The source's breathwork section names a second practice, Zensing (breath with sound, for connecting with emotions), which this guide doesn't mention; like Systema it is a breath practice in the source that may or may not belong in this section.
what: Same place as the Systema addition: whether Zensing gets a mention or a link.

hypnosis_quote: If you feel bad, dizzy, or panicky, or have medical issues, stop.
source_heading: Optional High-Intensity State-Shift and Release Practices
source_quote: Safety note: both of these methods are designed to produce lightheadedness, and both of them may be risky if you have heart disease.
why: The somatic guide also offers Vagal Blitz, a breath practice adapted from Wim Hof's and meant to make you lightheaded, while this passage says to breathe less and stop if dizzy; they are different practices with different aims, but a reader sent from here to the somatic guide's breathwork meets advice that runs the other way.
what: No sentence changes; if a link to the somatic guide's breathwork is added here, where it should point (the Buteyko passage or the whole guide).

hypnosis_quote: Work in this order – first your body, then your inner child, then some inquiry, then some action:
source_quote: I put Somatic Experiencing up at the beginning because it helps people to reconnect with their body, to begin to feel it again.
why: Under this sentence the guide runs breathing, EFT, Somatic Experiencing, Focusing, body supports, and the source runs breathwork, Somatic Experiencing, then EFT and massage a layer later, with a reason for putting Somatic Experiencing early.
what: The order of the EFT [S123] and Somatic Experiencing [S124] sections in the contents.

hypnosis_quote: Focusing is another approach where you work with your body.
source_heading: Layer 3: Compassionate Exploration of Trauma Feelings Before the Story Comes In
source_quote: After becoming more aware of bodily sensations and doing some cycles of crude discharge/settle, it’s time for some practices that can help you go deeper in a nuanced, loving and gentle way.
why: The live somatic guide has no passage on Focusing, Gendlin or the felt sense (the source quote only shows the layer where such a practice would sit), so this section has no source to be brought in line with, and the two files can't show whether the source ever had one.
what: The whole section [S125]: nothing to align; ask whether Focusing was cut from the somatic guide on purpose.
